limitations: One owned empty MREC v2019 table with one GSI; no sustained load or metric-triggered scaling tested.
Bounded observations do not establish AWS timing guarantees or entire replica autoscaling API parity.

AAS write clamp regional observation ended after 90 describe-pairs (roughly 10 minutes) without peer write capacity changing; script expectation of global write propagation failed and subsequent phases resumed separately.
CloudTrail lookup pages are bounded, not a complete account audit; original resource-filter queries reached page limits, while UpdateTable-filter queries preserve only owned table events.
Billing mode round trip restored historical scaling resources; new on-demand global table provisioned admission remains untested.
No standalone GSI all-same request, nondefault AAS suspension flags, explicit cooldown propagation, scheduled actions, or metric-driven scale-in/out tested.

creationPrerequisites.observation: An ACTIVE provisioned table with one ACTIVE provisioned GSI could not add a replica with no AAS, with only a table write target, with a table write policy but no GSI write target/policy, or with GSI write target but no GSI policy. Addition succeeded after both table and GSI had write scalable targets and target-tracking policies. Read autoscaling was not required.

errors.table: Table write capacity should either be Pay-Per-Request or AutoScaled.
errors.index: GSI write capacity should either be Pay-Per-Request or AutoScaled.

ordinaryCapacityPropagation.observation: Replica read overrides changed only peer table/GSI reads from 2/3 to 5/6. An all-same ordinary request was rejected on table unchanged-throughput validation and retained overrides. An accepted ordinary UpdateTable effectively changed only writes 2 to 3 while supplying required unchanged source reads 2/3: peer reads reset from 5/6 to 2/3 and writes became 3. Explicit source reads 4/5 then propagated to both regions. Required-but-unchanged fields DO reset peer overrides when that throughput update is accepted.
ordinaryCapacityPropagation.bounds: The combined all-same request failed on table validation; standalone GSI no-op validation was not isolated.

directAASRegistrationAndClamping.observation: RegisterScalableTarget in us-east-1 raised table/index write minimum from 1 to 4 and actual source writes 3 to 4. Peer writes remained 3 and peer reads8/9 remained overridden throughout 90 regional describe-pairs; source reads4/5 remained unchanged. Peer target minimum remained1 while source became4. Source read registration minima6/7 clamped source reads to6/7 but peer reads8/9 stayed unchanged; read targets and policies created directly in us-east-1 did not appear in us-east-2 within observed windows. Source scaling activities reported Successful min-capacity adjustments; no workload generated.

creationTimeScalingCopy.observation: Initial replica creation copied source table/GSI write targets and policies. Later removed the peer, removed leftover owned peer targets/policies, verified peer targets empty, and recreated peer. Recreated peer copied both table/GSI read and write settings: same PolicyName, MinCapacity/MaxCapacity, TargetValue, DisableScaleIn=true, RoleARN; SuspendedState remained all false; cooldown fields remained absent. Target identities/policy ARNs are regional, not reused ARNs. Reads min6/7, writes min5, max12 on both recreated replicas.
creationTimeScalingCopy.bounds: Nondefault suspended-state flags and explicit cooldown values were not tested.

replicaAutoScalingAPIScope.observation: DescribeTableReplicaAutoScaling returned both regions and table/GSI settings. UpdateTableReplicaAutoScaling with write min/max but no ScalingPolicyUpdate rejected the request even with existing write policies. Adding write policy configuration succeeded: writes min5 and actual W5 in both regions; peer-only read settings min10/11 and actual R10/11; source reads retained6/7. This API coordinated regional AAS settings, unlike direct regional RegisterScalableTarget/PutScalingPolicy.
replicaAutoScalingAPIScope.bounds: Only these concrete update shapes observed, not broad API parity.

cloudTrailCapacityActor.observation: Successful east1 AAS clamp events invokedBy dynamodb.application-autoscaling.amazonaws.com used UpdateTable with both dimensions, not ReplicaUpdates: 19:55:16Z table R4W4, 19:55:17Z GSI R5W4; 20:05:54Z table R6W4 and 20:05:55Z GSI R7W4. These service-actor updates remained regional despite ordinary caller updates propagating. Replica-autoscaling API later emitted regional AAS UpdateTable calls in both regions; east2 had recorded ResourceInUseException/ThrottlingException attempts before successful final capacities.
cloudTrailCapacityActor.credentialHandling: CloudTrail credential identifiers redacted before any file persistence. EventName-based pages retain only events whose requestParameters.tableName is the owned table.

billingModeHistoryBound.observation: Provisioned to on-demand transition succeeded. Both regions showed no visible owned targets/policies before returning to provisioned. Return to provisioned R2W2 table/GSI succeeded and settled in both regions, but previous AAS targets/policies reappeared by cleanup, requiring explicit final deletion.
billingModeHistoryBound.uncertainty: This history-dependent restoration does not establish that a never-provisioned global table lacking any autoscaling history can enter provisioned without write autoscaling. No general transition admission rule inferred.

productionBoundaries: Require provisioned table and each provisioned GSI write target plus target-tracking policy before replica creation; do not invent read-AAS prerequisite.
Creation copies actual AAS-owned read/write targets/policies into peer scope. Native direct AAS settings changes remained regional within capture; do not fan out all subsequent AAS mutations.

Preserve ordinary accepted UpdateTable throughput propagation, including unchanged required opposite dimension. AAS capacity execution needs a typed regional path, not ordinary caller global propagation or user-agent/caller-string hacks.
Treat Describe/UpdateTableReplicaAutoScaling as separate coordination API ownership; evidence does not justify claiming unimplemented full parity.
Do not overgeneralize on-demand-to-provisioned admission from a table retaining prior autoscaling history.
